narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This means the system sees enough warning signs that you are more likely to depart than to stay with the organization.

Three factors shaped this prediction most strongly. First, your total years of professional experience had the largest influence, but it worked in your favor: having only 1–5 years of overall experience is common among people the model expects to stay, and this profile pulled the prediction toward keeping you. Unfortunately, the other two major drivers pointed the other way. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second strongest factor and pushed the outcome toward leaving. Finally, working in the “other” sector rather than medical or education also increased the likelihood of departure.

Taken together, the positive pull from your limited experience was not enough to outweigh the combination of external opportunities and sector-related patterns. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether stronger internal growth paths could reduce the appeal of outside offers. You, in turn, may want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding before making any decision.
